docs.title: pepdata
docs.text: pepdata ships amino-acid property tables and pairwise residue matrices (BLOSUM, PMBEC, contact energies), turns peptide sequences into n-gram feature vectors, and loads MHC-binding and T-cell assay tables from the IEDB. It is the OpenVax library for peptide-level reference data. It does not predict MHC binding; for that, see mhctools and mhcflurry. Property lookups work offline; IEDB tables require a download.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
python -m pip install pepdata

Python 3.11 or later is required.

docs.title: Look up a peptide's residue properties
docs.text:
from pepdata.amino_acid_properties import hydropathy

peptide = "ACD"
print([hydropathy[residue] for residue in peptide])

[1.8, 2.5, -3.5]

The values come from the shipped residue-property table. The dictionary maps single-letter residues to numeric values; it does not predict MHC binding or clinical immunogenicity. Use uppercase canonical residue letters. A missing letter raises KeyError.

docs.title: Find the interface you need
docs.text:
Task Module or object Single-residue properties pepdata.amino_acid_properties BLOSUM substitution matrices pepdata.blosum PMBEC and contact tables pepdata.pmbec, pepdata.residue_contact_energies Residue alphabets pepdata.amino_acid_alphabet, pepdata.reduced_alphabet N-gram features pepdata.PeptideVectorizer MHC-binding assay tables pepdata.iedb.mhc T-cell assay tables pepdata.iedb.tcell

See residue and pairwise tables, then peptide features and IEDB tables. The API reference follows those same tasks.

Older pepdata documentation placed the property tables in amino_acid and described a StringTransformer interface. The property dictionaries are in amino_acid_properties, and there is no StringTransformer class.

docs.title: pairwise_table
docs.text:
Read whitespace-delimited tables of amino-acid pair coefficients.

One parser serves the BLOSUM substitution matrices, the PMBEC matrix and the residue contact energy tables that ship in pepdata/matrices.

docs.title: parse_pairwise_table
docs.text:
parse_pairwise_table(text, column_order=None, coeff_type=float)

Parse the text of a table of pairwise amino-acid coefficients.

Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.

Parameters:

  • text (str) –

    Contents of the table.

  • column_order (sequence of str, default: None ) –

    Residue labels of a table that has no header line and no row labels, such as the residue contact energy tables. The same labels name the rows and the columns, so the table must be square. When omitted, the first line holds the column labels and every later line starts with its row label.

  • coeff_type (callable, default: float ) –

    Converts each coefficient string to a number, e.g. int for BLOSUM scores.

Returns:

  • dict of str to dict of str to number –

    Coefficients accessed like table[row_label][column_label].

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the table is empty, a label is repeated, a row has the wrong number of fields, or a coefficient is not a number.

docs.text:
read_pairwise_table(path, column_order=None, coeff_type=float)

Read a file holding a table of pairwise amino-acid coefficients.

Parameters:

  • path (str or path - like) –

    Location of the table.

  • column_order (sequence of str, default: None ) –

    Residue labels of a table without a header line or row labels; see parse_pairwise_table.

  • coeff_type (callable, default: float ) –

    Converts each coefficient string to a number.

Returns:

  • dict of str to dict of str to number –

    Coefficients accessed like table[row_label][column_label].

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the table is malformed; see parse_pairwise_table.

docs.title: rekey_pairwise_table
docs.text:
rekey_pairwise_table(table, key_type='row')

Convert a nested pairwise table to one of the legacy key layouts.

Exists to support the deprecated key_type argument of pepdata.blosum.parse_blosum_table and pepdata.pmbec.read_pmbec_coefficients.

Parameters:

  • table (dict of str to dict of str to number) –

    Coefficients accessed like table[row_label][column_label].

  • key_type ((row, pair, pair_string), default: 'row' ) –

    'row' returns the nested layout unchanged, 'pair' keys each coefficient by a (row_label, column_label) tuple and 'pair_string' by the two labels joined into one string.

Returns:

  • dict –

    The coefficients in the requested layout.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If key_type is not one of the three layouts.

docs.text:
parse_blosum_table(table, coeff_type=int, key_type='row')

Parse a table of pairwise amino acid coefficient (e.g. BLOSUM50)

Deprecated since 1.3.8: use pepdata.pairwise_table.parse_pairwise_table or pepdata.pairwise_table.read_pairwise_table. This wrapper will be removed in a future release.

Parameters:

  • table (str) –

    Contents of a table with a header line of column labels.

  • coeff_type (callable, default: int ) –

    Converts each coefficient string to a number.

  • key_type ((row, pair, pair_string), default: 'row' ) –

    Layout of the returned dictionary; see pepdata.pairwise_table.rekey_pairwise_table.

Returns:

  • dict –

    Coefficients in the requested layout.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the table is malformed, has fewer than 20 column labels, or key_type is unknown.

docs.title: read_pmbec_coefficients
docs.text:
read_pmbec_coefficients(key_type='row', verbose=False, filename=PMBEC_PATH)

Read the PMBEC coefficient matrix.

Deprecated since 1.3.8: use pepdata.pairwise_table.read_pairwise_table. This wrapper will be removed in a future release.

Parameters:

  • key_type (str, default: 'row' ) –

    'row' : every key is a single amino acid, which maps to a dictionary for that row 'pair' : every key is a tuple of amino acids 'pair_string' : every key is a string of two amino acid characters

  • verbose (bool, default: False ) –

    Ignored. Earlier releases printed the header and residue list to stdout by default; nothing is printed any more.

  • filename (str, default: PMBEC_PATH ) –

    Location of PMBEC coefficient matrix

Returns:

  • dict –

    Coefficients in the requested layout.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the table is malformed, does not have exactly 20 columns, or key_type is unknown.

docs.title: parse_interaction_table

parse_interaction_table(table, amino_acid_order=CONTACT_TABLE_AMINO_ACID_ORDER)

Parse a headerless 20x20 table of residue contact energies.

Deprecated since 1.3.8: use pepdata.pairwise_table.parse_pairwise_table with its column_order argument. This wrapper will be removed in a future release.

Parameters:

  • amino_acid_order (str, default: CONTACT_TABLE_AMINO_ACID_ORDER ) –

Returns:

    Coefficients accessed like d[row_letter][column_letter].

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If the table does not have one row per residue or a row has the wrong number of coefficients.

docs.title: fit_transform
docs.text:
fit_transform(amino_acid_strings)

Learn the n-gram vocabulary of the given sequences and vectorize them.

Parameters:

  • amino_acid_strings (list of str) –

    Peptide or protein sequences.

Returns:

  • ndarray –

    Array of shape (len(amino_acid_strings), number of distinct n-grams) with n-gram counts, or per-row frequencies (each row divided by its total) when normalize_row is True.

docs.title: transform
docs.text:
transform(amino_acid_strings)

Vectorize sequences with the vocabulary learned by fit.

n-grams that weren't seen during fitting are not counted. Input sequences are unreduced, even when training_already_reduced was used during fitting.

Parameters:

  • amino_acid_strings (list of str) –

    Peptide or protein sequences.

Returns:

  • ndarray –

    Array of shape (len(amino_acid_strings), size of the fitted vocabulary), normalized per row as in fit_transform.

docs.title: Documentation style
docs.text:
Follow the PyEnsembl writing guide and the mhctools example.

Put installation and the first useful example on the home page. Give complete imports and concrete inputs, explain the result, and state prerequisites before the reader runs a command. Show output only when it has been checked. Label replaceable paths and templates.

Order guides by common tasks before advanced setup and implementation details. Keep desktop sidebar groups expanded initially and individually collapsible. Split a page when a substantial task or reference needs its own explanation. Preserve useful old links and anchors when moving content.

Use ordinary text for concepts and library names; reserve inline code for literal commands, API names, parameters, paths and values. Keep qualifications, experimental status and scientific limitations beside the claims they qualify.

Use system fonts, a readable line length and restrained headings. Let wide tables and code blocks scroll inside their containers. Avoid repetitive navigation lists in prose and excessive callouts.

Install requirements-docs.txt and run ./docs.sh before opening a PR. Review the home page and a reference page at desktop and narrow widths. Run the repository's required lint and test commands and execute complete examples. Documentation dependencies are separate from runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Peptide features and IEDB tables
docs.text: This guide covers turning peptides into n-gram count vectors and loading the IEDB's MHC-binding and T-cell assay tables, which need a download.

docs.title: N-gram features
docs.text:
from pepdata import PeptideVectorizer

vectorizer = PeptideVectorizer(max_ngram=2, normalize_row=False)
counts = vectorizer.fit_transform(["SIINFEKL", "SIINFEKV"])
print(counts.shape)
print(vectorizer.transform(["SIINFEKA"]).sum())

(2, 16)
13.0

PeptideVectorizer fits a vocabulary of residue n-grams, then transforms new sequences using that vocabulary. max_ngram controls the largest n-gram, so the two 8-mers above give 16 distinct 1- and 2-grams. transform() counts only n-grams seen during fitting: SIINFEKA has 15, but A and KA are new. Fit before calling transform(). These are sequence features, not binding predictions.

normalize_row=True, the default, divides each row by its total so the features are frequencies; the example passes normalize_row=False to show raw counts. Both settings return a NumPy array with one row per sequence.

docs.title: Load assay data
docs.text:
These templates require network access on the first use and can download large IEDB exports:

from pepdata.iedb import mhc, tcell

binding_assays = mhc.load_dataframe()
tcell_assays = tcell.load_dataframe()

By default, both loaders keep only peptides made of the 20 standard amino acids (only_standard_amino_acids=True). The loader reference lists the other filtering arguments, such as mhc_class, hla and human_only.

The MHC-binding and T-cell tables represent different assays. A positive binding measurement is not automatically a positive T-cell response. Preserve assay, species and allele metadata when selecting records; the IEDB is the upstream data source.

Each module exposes download(force=False) and local_path(auto_download=True). Call download() to fetch the export before loading a table, for example when preparing an environment. force=True requests a refresh; a cached export is a snapshot and does not by itself identify a pinned IEDB release.

Each load_dataframe() call reads the current local export and returns an independent DataFrame. Editing a returned frame does not affect later calls. After download(force=True), the next load reads the refreshed file. mhc.delete() and tcell.delete() remove their local exports without network access; deleting an absent export is a no-op. A later load downloads it again.

The allele catalogue loaders likewise return fresh lists, dictionaries and synonym sets on each call. Network reuse is handled by the on-disk cache.

docs.title: Residue and pairwise tables
docs.text: This guide shows how to read the property tables and pairwise matrices that ship with pepdata, and how to choose a residue alphabet. All of it works offline.

docs.title: Read a single-residue property
docs.text:
from pepdata.amino_acid_properties import hydropathy, volume

print(hydropathy["A"])
print(volume["A"])

1.8
91.5

Each table is a dictionary. Keep the scale and source context with the values when using them as features; the numbers from different properties are not interchangeable measurements.

docs.title: Read a pairwise coefficient
docs.text:
from pepdata.blosum import blosum62_dict

print(blosum62_dict["A"]["A"])

4

The first and second keys select the two residue letters. The exported NumPy matrices are 20 by 20 in canonical_amino_acid_letters order; extra symbols in the source dictionaries do not add empty rows or columns. BLOSUM tables and the other pairwise matrices describe different quantities; consult the shipped matrix and its original source before interpreting coefficients.

docs.title: Read a pairwise table from a file
docs.text:
read_pairwise_table is the parser behind every shipped pairwise matrix. A table with a header line of column labels and a label at the start of each row needs only its path:

from os.path import join

from pepdata.pairwise_table import read_pairwise_table
from pepdata.static_data import MATRIX_DIR

blosum62 = read_pairwise_table(join(MATRIX_DIR, "BLOSUM62"), coeff_type=int)
print(blosum62["W"]["W"])

11

The residue contact energy tables have neither a header nor row labels, so pass the residue order as column_order:

contact = read_pairwise_table(
    join(MATRIX_DIR, "helix_vs_coil.txt"),
    column_order="ARNDCQEGHILKMFPSTWYV")
print(contact["A"]["R"])

1.17

Malformed tables raise ValueError. The older parse_blosum_table, read_pmbec_coefficients and parse_interaction_table still work but emit a DeprecationWarning and will be removed in a future release.

docs.title: Use alphabets explicitly
docs.text: canonical_amino_acid_letters describes the standard residue alphabet. Extended and reduced alphabets are separate interfaces: do not assume every ambiguous letter has a value in every property table. Select and document an encoding policy before processing ambiguous sequences.
